title: Heaven cannot contain thee (1 Kings 8:27)
hook: Solomon's dedication prayer admits no house can hold God

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Temple went up in quiet, no barzel heard. Your line was finished before anyone hears it. Today the house is done, and its builder says it isn't big enough.

The building is finished. Cedar walls, gold, the ark carried up into the inner room. Then a cloud fills the house, and the text says the priests couldn't stand to minister because of it. Solomon stands before the altar, in front of the whole gathering of Israel, spreads his hands toward heaven, and begins to pray. It's the moment the whole project was for. And partway through the prayer, he asks a question that seems to undercut the very house he's standing in.
screen: `THE CLOUD FILLS THE HOUSE.` → `HANDS SPREAD TOWARD HEAVEN.` → `A QUESTION IN THE PRAYER.`

segments.voice: Will God really dwell on the earth? Solomon answers himself, in the 1917 Jewish Publication Society translation: "heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain Thee; how much less this house that I have builded!" Heaven of heavens: heaven beyond heaven. The Hebrew word for heaven is shamayim. So at the dedication of the Temple, its builder says the Temple can't hold God. Not even the sky can. Then why build it? The prayer answers in its own way. Again and again, Solomon asks that God's eyes be open toward this house, and that when people pray toward this place, God will hear from heaven. The house isn't a container. It's more like an address: a place to turn toward. Jewish tradition kept that idea after the Temple was gone. The Talmud teaches that someone praying turns toward the land of Israel, toward Jerusalem, toward the place where the house stood. A place can matter deeply and still not hold what it points to. A kitchen where someone you loved used to cook isn't that person, but you might stand in it a little longer than you need to. Solomon builds the house and, in the same breath, refuses to shrink God to fit it.
screen: `WILL GOD DWELL ON THE EARTH?` · `HEAVEN OF HEAVENS CANNOT CONTAIN.` · `NOT A CONTAINER: AN ADDRESS.` · `TURN TOWARD THE PLACE.` · then, large: `HOW MUCH LESS THIS HOUSE THAT I HAVE BUILDED.`

segments.voice: If a place feels holy to you, a synagogue, a corner of your home, a path you walk, let it come to mind, then let the picture widen: the room, the street, the city, the sky, and past the sky, what Solomon called the heaven of heavens. If you pray, you can turn toward a place and still let your prayer be bigger than it; if you don't, just sit with how large the space around you is.
Shamayim. The Hebrew word for heaven, which Solomon said even the heaven of heavens could not contain. Today's word.
Your line: a place to turn toward. A house can point to God without holding God. Day seven hundred sixty.

howItsDone: Jews read Solomon's dedication prayer in the book of Kings, and the Talmud teaches that one who prays should turn toward the land of Israel, toward Jerusalem and the place where the Temple stood.

Because prayer only counts if it's said inside the Temple's own walls.
